text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 5.3% today after crude oil prices tumbled below $100 per barrel—a sharp reversal from the stock's four-day rally that had pushed it up nearly $30. The drop came as traders interpreted Trump's openness to talks with Iran as a sign that geopolitical tensions in the Middle East might ease, reducing the risk of further supply disruptions and the tight market conditions that had been supporting oil prices higher earlier in the week.

The timing matters: MPC had been riding a wave of escalating Mideast crisis fears—Houthi attacks, the Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown, and the Strait of Hormuz closure all pushed crude up to $130 globally and supported refiner margins. Today's pivot toward potential diplomacy undercut that tailwind, even though refineries are still running near full capacity (96.8%) and U.S. oil storage remains relatively lean, which would normally support prices and refiner profitability.
